'''Aleksei Nikolaevich Parshin'''{{Efn|His name is sometimes romanized as '''Alexey''' or '''Aleksey'''<ref name="sixtieth-intro"/> and '''Paršin'''.<ref name="thesis"/>}} ({{langx|ru|Алексей Николаевич Паршин}}; 7 November 1942 – 18 June 2022) was a Russian mathematician, specializing in [[arithmetic geometry]]. He is most well-known for his role in the proof of the [[Mordell conjecture]].

==Education and career==
Parshin entered the Faculty of Mathematics and Mechanics of [[Moscow State University]] in 1959 and graduated in 1964.<ref name="seventieth"/><ref name="ae-CV"/> He then enrolled as a graduate student at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]], where he received his ''[[Candidate of Sciences|Kand. Nauk]]'' (Ph.D.) in 1968 under [[Igor Shafarevich]].<ref name="ae-CV">{{cite web |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Parshin_Alexey/CV |title=Alexey Parshin – Curriculum Vitae |website=[[Academia Europaea]] |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref><ref name="thesis">{{cite journal|last=Paršin |first=A. N. |title=Algebraic curves over function fields. |language=Russian |journal=Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR |volume=183 |year=1968 |issue=5 |pages=524–526|doi=10.1070/IM1968v002n05ABEH000723 |bibcode=1968IzMat...2.1145P }}</ref> In 1983, he received his ''[[Doctor Nauk]]'' (doctorate of sciences) from Moscow State University.<ref name="sixtieth-intro"/><ref name="ae"/>

Parshin became a junior research fellow at the Steklov Institute of Mathematics in Moscow in 1968, later becoming a senior and leading research fellow.<ref name="ae"/><ref name="seventieth"/> He became the head of its Department of Algebra in 1995.<ref name="ae"/><ref name="seventieth"/> He also taught at Moscow State University.<ref name="seventieth">{{cite journal |first1=Sergei V. |last1=Vostokov |first2=Sergey O. |last2=Gorchinskiy |first3=Alexander B. |last3=Zheglov |first4=Yurii G. |last4=Zarkhin |first5=Yuri V. |last5=Nesterenko |first6=Dmitri O. |last6=Orlov |first7=Denis V. |last7=Osipov |first8=Vladimir L. |last8=Popov |first9=Armen G. |last9=Sergeev |first10=Igor R. |last10=Shafarevich |title=Aleksei Nikolaevich Parshin (on his 70th birthday) |journal=[[Russian Mathematical Surveys]] |volume=68 |issue=1 |pages=189–197 |year=2013 |doi=10.1070/RM2013v068n01ABEH004827|bibcode=2013RuMaS..68..189V |s2cid=123001679 }}</ref>

==Research==
{{see also|Parshin chain|Parshin's conjecture}}
In his 1968 thesis, Parshin proved that the [[Mordell conjecture]] is a logical consequence of [[Faltings' theorem#Proofs|Shafarevich's finiteness conjecture]] concerning isomorphism classes of [[abelian variety|abelian varieties]] via what is known as ''Parshin's trick'', which gives an embedding of an [[algebraic curve]] into the [[Siegel modular variety]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Algebraic curves over function fields I|last=Parshin|first=A. N.|authorlink=Aleksei Parshin|journal=[[Izvestiya: Mathematics|Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat.]]|volume=32|year=1968|issue=5|pages=1191–1219|doi=10.1070/IM1968v002n05ABEH000723|bibcode=1968IzMat...2.1145P}}</ref><ref name="Cornell-Silverman">{{cite book|title=Arithmetic geometry. Papers from the conference held at the University of Connecticut, Storrs, Connecticut, July 30 – August 10, 1984 |editor1-last=Cornell | editor1-first=Gary | editor2-link=Joseph Hillel Silverman| editor2-last=Silverman | editor2-first=Joseph H. |year=1986 |publisher=Springer-Verlag |location= New York |isbn=0-387-96311-1 | doi=10.1007/978-1-4613-8655-1 | mr=861969}}</ref> Shafarevich proved his finiteness conjecture for the case with genus ''g''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1. Parshin proved a special case (for {{math|''S''}} = the empty set) of the following theorem: If {{math|''B''}} is a smooth complex curve and {{math|''S''}} is a finite subset of {{math|''B''}} then there exist only finitely many families (up to isomorphism) of smooth curves of fixed genus ''g''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;2 over {{math|''B'' \ ''S''}}.<ref name=CaporasoRef>{{cite arXiv|eprint=math/0004078|title=Remarks about uniform boundedness of rational points over function fields|last=Caporaso|first=Lucia|authorlink=Lucia Caporaso |year=2000 }}</ref> The general case (for non-empty {{math|''S''}}) of the preceding theorem was proved by [[Suren Arakelov]] in 1971.<ref name=CaporasoRef/><ref>{{cite arXiv|eprint=math/0311085 |author=Heier, Gordon|title=Uniformly effective Shafarevich conjecture on families of hyperbolic curves over a curve with prescribed degeneracy condition |year=2003}}</ref> At the same time, Parshin gave a new proof (without an application of the Shafarevich finiteness condition) of the Mordell conjecture in function fields (already proved by [[Yuri Manin]] in 1963 and by [[Hans Grauert]] in 1965).<ref>Parshin, [http://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=im&paperid=2513&option_lang=eng Algebraic curves over function fields. I], Math. USSR Izvestiya Vol. 2, 1968</ref> In 1983, [[Gerd Faltings]] completed the program and proved Shafarevich's finiteness conjecture, thereby proving the Mordell conjecture.<ref name="Cornell-Silverman"/>

His other research dealt with generalizations of [[class field theory]] in higher dimensions, with integrable systems, and with the history of mathematics.<ref name="sixtieth-intro">{{cite book |title=Algebraic Number Theory and Algebraic Geometry: Papers Dedicated to A. N. Parshin on the Occasion of his Sixtieth Birthday |editor1-first=Esther V. |editor1-last=Forbes |editor2-first=S. V. |editor2-last=Vostokov |editor2-link=Sergei Vostokov |editor3-first=Yuri |editor3-last=Zarhin |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |year=2002 |volume=300 |series=Contemporary Mathematics |isbn=0821832670 |doi=10.1090/conm/300 |page=vii–viii}}</ref><ref name="seventieth"/>

He was an editor for the Russian edition of the collected works of [[David Hilbert]] and was a co-editor, with [[Vladimir Arnold|V. I. Arnold]], of selected works of [[Hermann Weyl]].<ref name="sixtieth-intro"/><ref>{{cite book |editor1-first=Vladimir |editor1-last=Arnold |editor1-link=Vladimir Arnold |editor2-first=Aleksei |editor2-last=Parshin |title=Hermann Weyl, Selected Papers, Mathematics, Theoretical Physics |publisher=[[Nauka (publisher)|Nauka]] |location=Moscow |year=1984}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Parshin was born on 7 November 1942 in [[Yekaterinburg|Sverdlovsk]]<ref name="sixtieth-intro"/><ref name="seventieth"/> and died on 18 June 2022.<ref name="ae"/><ref name="steklov">{{cite web |url=http://www.mi-ras.ru/index.php |title=Mathematical Institute V.A. Steklov Russian Academy of Sciences |website=[[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] |access-date=18 June 2022 |language=ru |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220620110131/http://www.mi-ras.ru/index.php |archive-date=20 June 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="steklov-obit">{{cite web |url=http://www.mi-ras.ru/news/22/Parshin_obituary.pdf |title=Алексей Николаевич ПАРШИН |trans-title=Aleksei Nikolaevich Parshin |website=[[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] |access-date=21 June 2022 |language=ru}}</ref>

Parshin was longtime friends with Russian philosopher [[Aleksei Losev]] and started the Russian philosophy seminar at the Dom Loseva Library in Moscow.<ref name="domloseva">{{cite web |url=http://domloseva.ru/events/news/filosofiya/aleksej-nikolaevich-parshin-akademik-ran-vechnaya-pamyat |website=Dom Loseva Library |title=Алексей Николаевич Паршин, академик РАН. Вечная память! |trans-title=Alexei Nikolaevich Parshin, Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences. Everlasting memory! |date=21 June 2022 |access-date=22 June 2022 |language=ru}}</ref> Parshin was [[Eastern Orthodoxy|Orthodox Christian]] and wrote about the relationship between Russian religious philosophy and the modern sciences.<ref name="domloseva"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 1971, Parshin received the Prize of the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]] for young mathematicians.<ref name="ae"/> He was awarded the [[Humboldt Prize]] in 1996.<ref name="seventieth"/><ref name="ae"/> He received the [[Named prizes and medals of the Russian Academy of Sciences#Mathematics|Vinogradov Prize]] in 2004 and the [[Named prizes and medals of the Russian Academy of Sciences#Mathematics|Chebyshev Gold Medal]] in 2012 from the Russian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="seventieth"/><ref name="ae"/>

The [[Université Paris-Nord]] granted Parshin an honorary doctorate in 2001.<ref name="ae"/><ref name="sixtieth-intro"/> Parshin was elected a corresponding member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 2006 and then a full member in 2011.<ref name="ae"/> He was elected a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2017.<ref name="ae">{{cite web |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Parshin_Alexey |title=Parshin Alexey |website=[[Academia Europaea]] |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref>

Parshin was an invited speaker at the 1970 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) with his talk titled ''Quelques conjectures de finitude en géométrie diophantienne''.<ref name="ae"/><ref>Paršin, A. N. [http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1970.1/Main/icm1970.1.0467.0472.ocr.pdf "Quelques conjectures de finitude en géométrie Diophantienne."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924235505/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1970.1/Main/icm1970.1.0467.0472.ocr.pdf |date=24 September 2016 }} In Actes, Congrès intern. math, Tome 1, vol. 1, pp. 467–471. 1970.</ref> He was a plenary speaker at the 2010 ICM with his talk titled ''Representations of higher adelic groups and arithmetic''.<ref name="ae"/><ref>Parshin, A. N. [https://books.google.com/books?hl=en&lr=&id=GFE1vx2pynMC&pg=PA362 "Representations of higher adelic groups and arithmetic."] In Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, vol. 1, pp. 362–392. 2011.</ref>
